review.original_text: This is the same question as whether boolean formulas have polynomial size circuits.
review.response: The duplicate was already consolidated into TCS-0019. The nontrivial direction is whether polynomial-size circuits have polynomial-size formulas (equivalently nonuniform NC1 = P/poly); formulas themselves are already circuits. The original note is retained here with its former card ID.

review.original_text: A weaker version would be to prove that EXP has sub-exponential size circuits.
review.response: Added the suggested subexponential upper-bound variant and clarified its direction. It is weaker than EXP being contained in P/poly, not weaker than the opposite lower-bound conjecture asked on this card. The original main target is retained.

review.original_text: This is a simplification of the linear-sorting question on word-RAM. One would suspect that this could be solvable using current techniques.
review.response: Clarified the relation to ordinary integer sorting. This card asks about arbitrary exact reals on a real RAM, so a word-RAM integer-sorting algorithm alone does not settle it. The suggestion that current techniques may suffice remains a research judgment; no resolving algorithm was supplied.

editorial_responses_from_local_cards.card_title: Independence of P versus NP from ZFC

review.original_text: This is not a yes/no question. It depends on the proof system. I think for some very limited proof systems the answer is known to be that P vs NP is independent. Perhaps one would have to specify whether it is independent of say ZFC - Zernel-Frankl theroy with axion of choice.
review.response: Specified full ZFC, the arithmetic SAT sentence, finite formal derivability and the consistency convention. With the theory fixed this is a yes/no question. Results for weak theories are distinguished from independence of full ZFC.

editorial_responses_from_local_cards.card_title: Linear-size circuits for stable ternary compaction

review.original_text: This looks like a question within a reach of current techniques. Worth thinking about...
review.response: Retained the precisely stated stable ternary-compaction question. The cited results distinguish unstable compaction and conditional lower bounds from this unrestricted Boolean-circuit target. Possible tractability is an editorial assessment; the note supplies no theorem that resolves the problem.

review.original_text: One should check On the Complexity of Numerical Analysis by Eric Allender, Peter Bürgisser, Johan Kjeldgaard-Pedersen, and Peter Bro Miltersen
review.response: Read and added the recommended paper, distinguishing its Boolean-input results and constant conventions from this full real-input BSS question.

### Problem statement

Goal: Design an $O(1)$-approximation insertion-only streaming algorithm for estimating the minimum spanning tree (MST) cost in the $d$-dimension Euclidean space using one pass and space $\mathrm{poly}(d\cdot \log n)$, where $n$ is the number of points in the stream. Alternatively, show that no such algorithm is possible. (The dimension $d$ can be assumed to be logarithmic in $n$.)
